title: observability: token/KV cache metrics + tracing + dashboard/alert tuning
author: Maya Rao
description:
Motivation: We need finer-grained observability for token-level costs and KV cache behavior to diagnose regressions in tail latency and per-token cost spikes. This PR adds new Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing spans around KV cache operations, updates Grafana dashboards for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and tunes alert thresholds based on recent production traffic distributions.

Summary of changes: 1) Instrumentation: added token-level counters and histograms for tokens_emitted, tokens_charged (by model variant), kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, kv_fetch_latency_ms (histogram), and per_request_token_cost. Metrics are labeled by tenant_id, model, model_variant, route, and region. 2) Tracing: added spans around KV cache lookup, cache population, and fallback model routing; spans include attributes for cache_key, hit/miss, and size of KV payload (when available). Traces are sampled at 1% by default with a dynamic override for error/latency cases. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard panels for token-level cost breakdown, KV hit ratio heatmaps by route/model, and per-tenant 95/99 latency correlated with token counts. 4) Alerts: tuned existing alerts to reduce noise - replaced a single token-cost spike alert with a two-stage alert (warning if 95th token cost > baseline*2 for 10m, critical if > baseline*3 for 5m and accompanied by increased tail latency). Added a low-volume suppression rule to avoid noisy alerts from tiny tenants. 5) Backfills/migrations: added a short-lived job to backfill kv_hit_ratio for the last 7 days into the rolling window aggregators.

Checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus metric definitions and exposition in runtime instrumentation layer - [x] Add OTEL spans and hookup to the tracing exporter - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + templating vars (model, region, tenant) - [x] Alert rules with suppression and escalation windows - [x] Backfill job + migration notes - [x] Unit + integration tests for metric tags and span attributes - [x] Release notes and rollout plan

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover metric label consistency and API surface changes. Integration tests run a synthetic workload in staging that exercises KV cache hot/warm/cold paths and assert expected kv_cache_hits/misses and emitted spans. Staging dashboards were validated against 48h synthetic traffic; alerts were exercised using the alert_test harness. Observability team ran a 24-hour canary on a small subset of production traffic with dynamic sample rate at 5% to validate traces and metric cardinality.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag enable_observability_v2 (off by default). 2) Enable in canary (5% of traffic) for 24 hours and monitor cardinality and ingestion cost. 3) If stable, increase to 25% for 48 hours, then full rollout. 4) After 7 days of full traffic, run backfill job and remove temporary suppression.

Compatibility: All changes are additive. Metric names and labels follow existing conventions to avoid breaking downstream dashboards. The feature flag prevents accidental exposure.

Notes: Prometheus metrics include high-cardinality labels (tenant_id/model_variant) but we capped cardinality with a label_whitelist implemented in the runtime config; the canary validated there was no significant spike in metrics ingestion. Related: ENG-3214 (dashboard refresh), ENG-3301 (alert tuning), SUP-4521 (customer observed token-cost spike).
commits: feat(observability): add token-level metrics and KV cache histograms
feat(tracing): add spans for KV lookup/populate and fallback routing
chore(dashboards): add Grafana JSON + template vars for token cost and KV heatmaps
test(observability): integration tests for kv cache metrics and span attributes
docs: release notes and rollout plan
fix(ci): adjust integration matrix to include OTEL env
review_comments: Alex Kim: Left a couple of comments about label cardinality - please ensure tenant_id is replaced with tenant_bucket where appropriate to avoid high-cardinality explosion.
Maya Rao: Good catch - switched to tenant_bucket for non-enterprise tenants and added a whitelist for enterprise IDs. Updated tests to validate bucketing logic.
Samir Gupta: Can we reduce trace attribute size by avoiding embedding full cache_key in attributes? Concerned about PII/size.
Maya Rao: Will keep cache_key hash only (sha256) and added note to tracing.go. Confirmed no PII is emitted.
Priya Patel: Alert tuning looks reasonable; suggested adding suppression window for tiny tenants - added that change.
Alex Kim: CI flake on integration test reproed locally; fixed by increasing OTEL collector timeout and re-running tests. Verified green.
Samir Gupta: Approving - observed dashboard looks actionable; no further comments.
release_notes:
- Added token-level cost and latency metrics with KV cache hit/miss histograms.
- Added tracing spans around KV operations and fallback routing.
- New Grafana dashboard for token-level cost breakdown and KV heatmaps.
- Tuned alert thresholds and suppression rules to reduce noisy alerts.
- Backfill job to populate recent kv_hit_ratio for rolling aggregators.
notes: Monitored cardinality and ingestion cost during canary; increase in Prometheus ingestion was within acceptable limits (<5%). OTEL traces sampled at 1% default. Follow-up: consider adding adaptive sampling if trace volume rises.
migration_instructions: Run tools/backfill/kv_hit_backfill.py --days 7 --target rolling-window after full rollout. Ensure feature flag enable_observability_v2 is set for canary namespace before enabling in more namespaces.
